summary: Kirpal Singh's replies to individual initiates, the closest thing in his line to a case-book. Many letters respond to a specific report: darkness only, blue patches, a purple veil turning gold, sky with stars, white light seen at initiation and then lost, red or golden light, the Master seen in golden light. The standing advice: fix the inner gaze 'penetratingly' into the darkness between and behind the eyebrows with no strain on eyes or forehead and no awareness of breathing; keep looking into the middle of whatever is there, light or darkness; when stars appear pick out a big one and look into its middle until it gives way; do not visualise or try to pull the light closer. Lost or faded light is traced to strain, divided attention or lapses in conduct, and patience is urged.
why_relevant: Troubleshooting addressed to named experiences, including first light seen at initiation and lost afterwards; shows what the teacher says to those who see nothing and to those who see colours.

date_evidence.basis: Front matter of the saved text: 'Unity of Man - First edition 1993 / No rights reserved'. The first Ruhani Satsang edition (1967) is from memory and not verified here; the author died in 1974, so the content predates that.
